I knew going into this sink purchase that it was made for European/Asian specs.  As long as you know that and can logically find your own work-arounds, it is a beautiful sink!  The drain pipes are not US standard, nor is the display setting--it reads temperature in Celsius.  However, if you look at the few places that offer a standard US version, the prices are 2-3x higher.I did not find the bottom flimsy  (stated in a different review) and we were able to hook our old garbage disposal up to it.  The display is run by hydro-electric power, meaning that the water flowing through the faucet is literally what makes the display work.Most of the models similar to this one are the same way, so buyer beware. Here's an HONEST review, from a Redneck, with 2 daughters, and my wife using it (and occasionally myself). We've had it installed in my daughters' bathroom for about 2 months now and so far (knock on wood) it's been great (even being used MULTIPLE times a day).(PROS)You'll knotice right off the bat when you get it, that it seems build well.. (though I wish they made the removable sprayer metal as well... but good luck finding a metal one of those in the first place). Everything assembled easily, and there's plenty of height adjustment in the "rain" shower head. I'm 5'11", and adjusted it so I wash my hair, that when my elbows go above my head, they doesn't come close to touching the sprayer head. The removable sprayer has a LONG hose, witch is GREAT. It can actually reach to the back of the tub, which is awesome to spray cleaning the back side of the tub and back tiled wall (which is AMAZING with all the hair that seems to sheds off 3 females). And a happy bonus in our case, is that it's even long enough to reach our toilet, making cleaning the toilet EASY. And the removable sprayer has a good set of spraying options.(CONS)To be honest, there's only really 1 issue I have, and 2 things I just kinda wish were different. The (1st) thing I didn't like was the removable sprayer head wall mount. It's a stick on type holder. YES it's a really strong adhesive, it was super easy to mount, and seem fine. But I guess I'm just partial to a more permanent mount style. But if you're not about drilling holes in your tile or shower wall for a permanent placement, then you'll love it. (2nd) Like I mentioned before, I SO WISH the removable sprayer head was metal. But I've tried searching for a set like this with one, and it's virtually impossible (unless you're willing to pay quite a few hundred buck). (3rd) This last one is again more of a personal preference... I wish the removable sprayer had a single stream "jet" spay (like a high pressure garden hose has). It does have a concentrated spray setting, that has plenty of pressure. But I just personally like the single spray ability (though my wife says she couldn't care less).But other than that.. It's probably exactly what you're looking for. So YES... If you're looking to get a set like this, then I'd HIGHLY RECOMMEND this one. You'll be hard pressed to find another set for this price, build quality, features, adjustability, and looks. PLUS neither my wife OUR teenage daughters have gripped at me, or complained about the shower since I put it in. I'd pay 5x as much just for that alone. I ordered this TEAK SHOWER  STOOL for 3 reasons:1.  It was advertised to be made from TEAK wood.2.  Generous height and seat dimensions.3.  Attractive style.The stool arrived in 4 sections, along with instructions and hardware.  To my dismay, it took me over an hour to assemble a stool that should have taken no more than 5 minutes.  In fact, assembly was a downright nightmare!  Due to alignment issues with the four bolts that attach the bottom shelf to the side rails.  More specifically...❗️ The bolt holes in the shelf cleats were not “on-center” with the blind threaded nuts in the bottom shelf.  In fact, the alignment was so bad that in some instances less than one-half of the threads were visible through the bolt hole.❗️ The angle of the blind threaded nut did not always match the angle of the bolt holes.  As a result, the threads were prone to cross-threading during installation of the bolts.In the end, I was unable to install the bottom shelf without making a modification to one of the four holes.  That involved reaming the bolt hole with a 5/16” drill bit, then extending the one side with a rotary sanding bit.  Because this modification increased the size of the bolt hole, a larger size washer was required.In fairness, it’s possible that the assembly issues that I encountered are unique to the stool that I received.  Yet there’s another problem with this shower stool that may be more universal in nature.  It appears to be made from ACACIA wood, not TEAK as advertised.  I have several pieces of TEAK furniture, and to my eye, the grain pattern and density/hardness of the wood used for the shower stool just don’t agree.  But even more to the point, the box that the stool was packaged in at the factory is clearly labeled as “ACACIA WOOD” (see pics).I have to admit feeling a bit duped.  Had I known this stool was ACACIA I would have never ordered it.  Not because I don’t appreciate ACACIA.  Quite the contrary.  ACACIA wood is a very nice alternative to TEAK.  However, it does requires more attention to care compared to TEAK if the wood is used in a wet environment like a shower.  But the main reason I wouldn’t have ordered it is because of the price.  Currently listed at $69.99, that price might be appropriate for TEAK, but not for ACACIA.As much as I would like to recommend this product, it’s just too expensive for an ACACIA shower stool.  Still, it's very attractive and should work well in many applications.  But before buying, I would consider other more cost-effective options.

I was excited to receive this beautiful teak shower bench.  It came well packaged encased in foam for protection.  All the parts were enclosed and in good shape.  When I started putting it together the legs connected to the bench easily, AND THEN the issue.  As you can see from the one picture, the one leg was missing a hole through which a bolt is supposed to connect the leg to the bench.  Without that hole, the leg would only have one point of connection and thus weaken the entire structure.  I almost just set it aside and gave up but then the review which I promised to do would not have been as valid as it could have been, so I drilled a hole where the original hole was supposed to be so I could continue.  The hole drilled extremely hard and smoked so I am not sure how the legs were made but it should not have been as hard as it was.  Anyway, it went together and fits nicely into our shower and works just fine.  The screws are exposed to water and hopefully will withstand the moisture and not rust.  Only time will tell.  They are supposed to be stainless so should be ok, but I must admit I have some reservation about quality control given the absent leg hole that I had to drill.

I am actually using this table for an "off-label" purpose, it's on the deck rather than in the bathroom. But hey, if it can live in a shower it can live in rain, right? And on that front, it is doing fine, no issues getting wet causing any apparent damage. But some issues arose before that. First, during assembly on a faux hardwood floor, the varnish was easily scuffed. Now, it comes with a few little shower poofs and a bamboo soap dish, little extras but nothing huge. As for the assembly itself, six pieces to assemble, the four legs and two level surfaces. All held together by twelve screws. See where this is going? One of the holes was drilled at such a wonky angle I could not get the screw to thread in the leg. Now the top level, where the misaligned hole is, has two screws per leg, and I could either redrill the hole or just use one screw for that leg. Given having two holes sharing a terminus at one end and thirty degrees apart might end up with the screw offering minimal support, and that I intend to use it exclusively as a table and not a stool, I went with just one screw. Is it still stable? Yes. Will it's max weight be lower? Presumably but I don't intend to find out. So, simple furniture with water resistance/tolerance, good, quality control however, lackluster.
